_about: Quotations whose wording follows the Astor Library Edition where the record's source text reads differently (a misprint in the source, or a different reading). Each entry gives the source's own reading of the line; scripts/verify-quotations.js checks that reading against the source, so the quotation is still located there.

a-midsummer-nights-dream.double-cherry: So we grow together, Like to a double cherry, seeming parted, But yet an union in partition; Two lovely berries moulded on one stem;
a-midsummer-nights-dream.seasons-alter: And thorough this distemperature we see The seasons alter: hoary-headed frosts Far in the fresh lap of the crimson rose,

alls-well-that-ends-well.dark-house: War is no strife To the dark house and the detested wife.
alls-well-that-ends-well.lowest-place: From lowest place when virtuous things proceed, The place is dignified by the doer's deed.

henry-iv-part-1.life-times-fool: But thought's the slave of life, and life time's fool; And time, that takes survey of all the world, Must have a stop. O, I could prophesy, But that the earthy and cold hand of death Lies on my tongue: no, Percy, thou art dust And food for--

king-john.italian-priest: no Italian priest Shall tithe or toll in our dominions; But as we under God are supreme head, So, under Him, that great supremacy, Where we do reign, we will alone uphold

king-lear.cannot-heave-my-heart: Unhappy that I am, I cannot heave My heart into my mouth: I love your majesty According to my bond; nor more nor less.
king-lear.reason-not-the-need: O, reason not the need: our basest beggars Are in the poorest thing superfluous: Allow not nature more than nature needs, Man's life's as cheap as beast's:

macbeth.all-hail: All hail, Macbeth, thou shalt be king hereafter!
macbeth.neptunes-ocean: Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood Clean from my hand? No, this my hand will rather The multitudinous seas in incarnadine, Making the green one red.

measure-for-measure.doubts-are-traitors: Our doubts are traitors And make us lose the good we oft might win By fearing to attempt.
measure-for-measure.proud-man: but man, proud man, Drest in a little brief authority, Most ignorant of what he's most assured, His glassy essence, like an angry ape, Plays such fantastic tricks before high heaven As make the angels weep;

othello.farewell-the-tranquil-mind: Farewell the tranquil mind! farewell content! Farewell the plumed troop, and the big wars, That make ambition virtue!
othello.old-black-ram: Even now, now, very now, an old black ram Is topping your white ewe.

richard-ii.sea-walled-garden: When our sea-walled garden, the whole land, Is full of weeds, her fairest flowers choked up, Her fruit-trees all upturned, her hedges ruin'd, Her knots disorder'd and her wholesome herbs Swarming with caterpillars?
richard-ii.was-this-the-face: Was this the face that faced so many follies, And was at last out-faced by Bolingbroke? A brittle glory shineth in this face: As brittle as the glory is the face;

richard-iii.builds-his-hopes-in-air: O momentary grace of mortal men, Which we more hunt for than the grace of God! Who builds his hopes in air of your good looks, Lives like a drunken sailor on a mast, Ready, with every nod, to tumble down Into the fatal bowels of the deep.
richard-iii.fouler-toad: Never hung poison on a fouler toad. Out of my sight! thou dost infect my eyes.
richard-iii.naked-villany: And thus I clothe my naked villany With old odd ends stolen out of holy writ; And seem a saint, when most I play the devil.
richard-iii.openingLine: Now is the winter of our discontent Made glorious summer by this sun of York;
richard-iii.winter-of-discontent: Now is the winter of our discontent Made glorious summer by this sun of York; And all the clouds that lour'd upon our house In the deep bosom of the ocean buried.

romeo-and-juliet.profane-hand: If I profane with my unworthiest hand This holy shrine, the gentle fine is this: My lips, two blushing pilgrims, ready stand To smooth that rough touch with a tender kiss.
romeo-and-juliet.teach-the-torches: O, she doth teach the torches to burn bright! It seems she hangs upon the cheek of night Like a rich jewel in an Ethiope's ear; Beauty too rich for use, for earth too dear!

taming-of-the-shrew.curst-and-shrewd: Her eldest sister is so curst and shrewd That till the father rid his hands of her, Master, your love must live a maid at home;
taming-of-the-shrew.peace-it-bodes: Marry, peace it bodes, and love and quiet life, And awful rule and right supremacy; And, to be short, what not, that's sweet and happy?

the-merchant-of-venice.all-that-glitters: All that glitters is not gold; Often have you heard that told: Many a man his life hath sold But my outside to behold:

the-rape-of-the-lock-and-an-essay-on-cri.voice-of-fools: Of all the Causes which conspire to blind / Man's erring judgment, and misguide the mind, / What the weak head with strongest bias rules, / Is Pride, the never-failing voice of fools.

the-tempest.rarer-action: Though with their high wrongs I am struck to the quick, Yet with my nobler reason 'gaitist my fury Do I take part: the rarer action is In virtue than in vengeance
the-tempest.thing-of-darkness: Two of these fellows you Must know and own; this thing of darkness! Acknowledge mine.

the-two-gentlemen-of-verona.force-ye: I’ll woo you like a soldier, at arms’ end, And love you ’gainst the nature of love—force ye.

timon-of-athens.number-of-men-eats: O you gods, what a number of men eats Timon, and he sees 'em not! It grieves me to see so many dip their meat in one man's blood

titus-andronicus.baked-in-that-pie: Why, there they are, both baked in that pie, Whereof their mother daintily hath fed, Eating the flesh that she herself hath bred.

troilus-and-cressida.degree: Take but degree away, untune that string, And hark what discord follows! Each thing melts In mere oppugnancy
troilus-and-cressida.whore-and-cuckold: All the argument is a whore and a cuckold—a good quarrel to draw emulous factions and bleed to death upon.

twelfth-night.love-sought-is-good: Love sought is good, but given unsought better.

venus-and-adonis.hunting-he-loved: Rose-cheek’d Adonis tried him to the chase; Hunting he lov’d, but love he laugh’d to scorn;
